rejected_findings.title: B1 fix comment assumes 10.8px/glyph but the pipeline renders 8.156px @18 (~22px actual clearance)
rejected_findings.reason: The 8.156px figure contradicts this pipeline's measurements twice over: fontTools raw advance = 600/1000em = 10.8px @18, and MeasureTextEx semantics at spacing=1 give '100%' = 4x10.8+3 = 46.2px (r1's on-pipeline figure). The comment's 10.8px advance is CORRECT; its 12px clearance claim verified at 12.95px raw. Collision-freedom holds under every reading.

warnings.title: NEW (fix-commit): queue-row measure/draw twins diverge at amber_pct==0 — the >0 guard exists only in noc_queue_rows; draw_noc_panel:771 lacks it
warnings.evidence: measure: `if p.q[0]+p.q[1]+p.q[2] > 0 || (amber_pct > 0 && p.util_pct >= u32(amber_pct))` — draw: `if p.q[0]+p.q[1]+p.q[2] == 0 && p.util_pct < u32(amber_pct) { continue }`. At amber=0: measure counts only q>0 rows (the new test PINS this: noc_queue_rows(&sr,0)==1); draw never skips (util<u32(0) impossible) and renders EVERY pipe.
warnings.detail: Violates the file's own contract ('noc_panel_rows ... MUST agree with draw_noc_panel row-for-row'). Latent: shipped catalog pipe_amber_pct=70 (ODN-5 fail-fast), so production is unaffected; a catalog tune to 0 (disable-amber) would under-count the scroll clamp vs drawn rows. The PIPES twins got the guard on both sides; QUEUES got it on one. Six of seven lenses filed it.
warnings.recommended_fix: Mirror the guard at the draw site: `if p.q[0]+p.q[1]+p.q[2] == 0 && (amber_pct <= 0 || p.util_pct < u32(amber_pct)) { continue }`.
